SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p583/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p583/r1.speaker: النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p583/r1.claim: Grammarians treat the added lā in ‘good and evil are not equal’ as an emphatic particle.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p583/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p583/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p583/r2.claim: The extra lā also signals that good deeds differ among themselves, evil deeds differ among themselves, and good and evil differ; he applies this to 35:22 and 35:20.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p583/r2.anchor: زيادة (لا) تفيد أن الحسنات لا تستوي بين بعضها لأن بعض الحسنات أفضل وأعظم من بعض

DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.claim: Ḥamīm can mean a close relative or intimate friend.
DAMGHANI:v1p146/r5.anchor: فوجه منهما : الحميم القريب قوله تعالى في سورة المعارج

BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r1.speaker: ابن الفارض
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-Farid’s cited verse says one who wastes life has no share of its wine-like blessing.
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r1.anchor: على نفسه قليبك من ضاع عمره.

BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r2.claim: Some attain a share of this love but not fully; others never reach spiritual satiation, which is the state of perfection.
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r2.anchor: ومن الناس من له نصيب من هذا الأمر لكن لا على وجه الكمال

BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh wrote that love’s cup had intoxicated him; Abu Yazid replied that the strong keep drinking without exhausting the drink or becoming satiated, even after seven seas.
BURSEVI:v8p196#3/r3.anchor: حكي أن يحيى بن معاذ الرازي رضي الله عنه : كتب إلى أبي يزيد البسطامي

BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r1.claim: The verse encourages the Prophet to endure unbelievers’ harm and answer their wrongdoing with goodness; patient restraint merits esteem here and reward in the afterlife, unlike their evil conduct.
BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r1.anchor: بيان لمحاسن الأعمال الجارية بين العبد وبين الرب ترغيبا لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r2.claim: On the reading of good and evil as individual kinds, both vary internally—good deeds from removing harm upward, and sins from minor to major—so the second negating particle is not merely emphatic, as al-Kashshaf indicates.
BURSEVI:v8p200#2/r2.anchor: إذا فسرت الحسنة والسيئة بالجنس على أن يكون المعنى لا تستوي الحسنات إذ هي متفاوتة في أنفسها

BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r1.claim: Repel an enemy’s evil by the best available good, such as kindness to an offender; this exceeds simple forgiveness, and the command’s wording intensifies the call to answer with goodness.
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r1.anchor: ادفع السيئة حين اعترضتك من بعض أعاديك بالتي هي أحسن ما يمكن دفعها به من الحسنات كالإحسان إلى من أساء

BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r2.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r2.claim: The Prophet practiced what he taught: keep ties with one who cuts them, pardon the wrongdoer, and treat an offender well.
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r2.anchor: صل من قطعك واعف عمن ظلمك وأحسن إلى من أساء إليك

BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r3.claim: The phrase answers the question of how to repel evil; using the superlative ‘best’ makes the instruction stronger, since one who repels with the best can easily use a lesser good.
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r3.anchor: وضع أحسن موضع الحسنة ؛ لأنه أبلغ في الدفع بالحسنة

BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r4.claim: The result is that a hostile opponent becomes like a compassionate close friend.
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r4.anchor: فإذا فعلت ذلك صار عدوك المشاق

BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r5.claim: A report identifies Abu Sufyan ibn Harb as the occasion of revelation: after severe enmity, a marriage tie softened him toward Muslims, and his conversion made him a close ally through Islam and kinship.
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r5.anchor: روي : أنها نزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب ، وذلك أنه لان للمسلمين بعد الشدة

BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r6.speaker: الإمام الأعظم
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r6.claim: A Persian anecdote attributed to the Greatest Imam says that when someone spoke ill of him, he praised that person until the other began speaking well of him.
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r6.anchor: از امام اعظم نقلست كسى بمن رسانندكه مرابدمى كويد من درشان او سحن نيكو ترمى كويم

BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r7.speaker: البقلي
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r7.claim: Al-Baqli says good character differs from bad character; one should replace blameworthy traits with praiseworthy ones, especially forbearance, which turns enemies into friends and repays anger, oppression, and bad treatment with patience, pardon, and generosity.
BURSEVI:v8p200#3/r7.anchor: قال البقلي : بين الله ها هنا أن الخلق الحسن ليس كالخلق السيىء

QASHANI:41:34-35/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:34-35/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:34-35/r1.claim: Good arises from the heart and leads to paradise and angels; evil arises from the self and leads to hell and devils. Answer an enemy's evil with the best good, since evil for evil grows.
QASHANI:41:34-35/r1.anchor: الأولى من مقام القلب تجر صاحبها إلى الجنة ومصاحبة الملائكة، والثانية من مقام النفس

QASHANI:41:34-35/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:34-35/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:41:34-35/r2.claim: Answering with good quiets hostility, establishes the responder in the heart, guides to paradise, expels Satan, and can bring remorse; the best response reflects divine mercy and makes an enemy close.
QASHANI:41:34-35/r2.anchor: سكنت شرارته وأزلت عداوته وتثبت في مقام القلب على الخير، وهديت إلى الجنة وطردت الشيطان

QASHANI:41:34-35/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:41:34-35/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
QASHANI:41:34-35/r3.claim: Qashani attributes to the Prophet a saying that if the Creator could appear, He would appear as forbearance; no grading is given.
QASHANI:41:34-35/r3.anchor: لو جاز أن يظهر البارىء لظهر بصورة الحلم

QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r6.claim: Repel evil with what is better by forgiving rather than repaying, overlooking slips, and giving up retaliation; the enemy then resembles an intimate friend without becoming fully sincere.
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r6.anchor: بالعفو عن المكافأة ، وبالتجاوز والصفح عن الزلة ، وترك الانتصاف

QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r7.claim: This is good conduct in serving God: bear patiently with His servants for His sake, and do not avenge yourself on people.
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r7.anchor: تحلم مع عباده لأجله . ومن جملة حسن الخلق في الصحبة مع الخلق

QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r8.claim: Only those granted patience can reach these virtues and rise from base traits; the highest ranks require enduring hardship.
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r8.anchor: لا يقوم بحق هذه الأخلاق إلا من أكرم بتوفيق الصبر

QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r11.claim: The revealed signs make the proofs clear and remove the excuse of anyone seeking the way to God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p151/r11.anchor: أوضح الآيات ، وألاح البينات ، وأزاح علة من رام الوصول

SULAMI:v2p219/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p219/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p219/r1.claim: Bad manners in intimate service are more serious than bad manners at a distance: God may overlook ignorant people's grave sins but catches the truthful for glances and distractions.
SULAMI:v2p219/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لا يستوي بين من احسن الدخول في خدمتنا والخروج منها وبين من اساء الأدب في الخدمة

AKHFASH:v2p507/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p507/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p507/r2.claim: The repeated ولا is permissible when both coordinated subjects fail to be equal, as in لا يستوي عبد الله ولا زيد.
AKHFASH:v2p507/r2.anchor: وقال {ولا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة} وقد يجوز، لأنك تقول: "لا يستوي عبد الله ولا زيد"

AKHFASH:v2p507/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p507/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p507/r3.claim: Alternatively, the second لا is emphatic and can be omitted; he compares لئلا يعلم and لا أقسم.
AKHFASH:v2p507/r3.anchor: وان شئت قلت ان الثانية زائدة تريد: لا يستوي عبد الله وزيد. فزيدت [لا] توكيدا كما قال {لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب} أي: لأن يعلم. وكما قال {لا أقسم بيوم القيامة}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p286/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p286/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p286/r6.claim: The promise is God's own concluding praise of those who affirm and uphold their Lord, not continued angelic speech; it establishes their entitlement and exposes the gulf from disbelievers who told others not to listen to Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p286/r6.anchor: ليس هذا من حكاية خطاب الملائكة للمؤمنين في الآخرة وإنما هو موجه من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r4.claim: One possible connection joins 41:34 to the praise in 41:33: the believer's good condition contrasts with the disbeliever's evil, like the comparison in 40:58.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r4.anchor: عطف هذه الجملة له موقع عجيب ، فإنه يجوز أن يكون عطفا على جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r5.claim: Alternatively, it reconnects to the disbelievers' call to ignore Quran, consoling the Prophet against their refusal and preparing the command to respond well.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p289/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون عطفا على جملة { وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرءان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r1.claim: Goodness includes every virtue, especially inviting people to Islam and overlooking their rude rejection; pardon avoids inflaming religious zeal and can soften receptive hearts, preparing the command to answer in the best way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r1.anchor: فالحسنة تعم جميع أفراد جنسها وأولاها تبادرا إلى الأذهان حسنة الدعوة إلى الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r2.claim: Denying equality usually praises one side over the other; the verse's repeated لا either reinforces negation or compresses both directions of comparison, fully excluding equality between good and evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r2.anchor: فكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال : ولا تستوي الحسنة والسيئة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r3.claim: The repeated negation can imply an omitted reciprocal phrase, neither good equaling evil nor evil equaling good, making the contrast complete rather than hyperbolic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r3.anchor: وأحسن من اعتبار التأكيد أن يكون في الكلام إيجاز حذف مؤذن باحتباك في الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r4.claim: Using the abstract nouns الحسنة والسيئة rather than doer nouns portrays each side as reaching the full extent of goodness or evil and leads into ethical counsel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p290/r4.anchor: وفي التعبير بالحسنة والسيئة دون المحسن والمسيء إشارة إلى أن كل فريق من هذين قد بلغ الغاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r1.claim: The imperative either follows the contrast as its practical consequence, or concludes the preceding argument; in both readings it stands independently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r1.anchor: جملة { ادفع بالتي هي أحسن } مفصولة غير معطوفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r2.claim: The Prophet was commanded to complete human moral excellence; ʿĀʾisha described his character as the Qurʾan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r2.anchor: وإنما أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك لأن منتهى الكمال البشري خلقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r3.claim: Excellence is intrinsically good, but for legal limits such as punishment foregoing it can be praiseworthy; pursue it unless a greater excellence is at risk.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r3.anchor: والكمال مطلوب لذاته فلا يعدل عنه ما استطاع ما لم يخش فوات كمال أعظم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet never avenged himself, except when God's inviolable limits were violated, then he acted for God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r4.anchor: ما انتقم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنفسه قط إلا أن تنتهك حرمات الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r5.claim: The community is encouraged to this disposition, linked to the promise that whoever pardons and makes amends has reward with God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r5.anchor: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r6.claim: A report through ʿIyāḍ, Ibn Mardawayh, Jābir, and Ibn Jarīr says that, after 7:199, Gabriel conveyed God's command to maintain kinship, give to the deprived, and pardon the wrongdoer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r6.anchor: وروى عياض في ( الشفاء ) وهو مما رواه ابن مردويه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r7.claim: The omitted object of “repel” is the evil deed, supplied by the contrast: repel evil with the best deed, as in parallel verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p291/r7.anchor: فلما أمر بأن تكون الحسنة مدفوعا بها تعين أن المدفوع هو السيئة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r1.claim: “That which is best” means a good deed; its superlative form encourages responding well because anger naturally inclines people to retaliate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r1.anchor: وإنما صيغت بصيغة التفضيل ترغيبا في دفع السيئة بها لأن ذلك يشق على النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r2.claim: The Prophet is described as never answering evil with evil, but pardoning and overlooking; this was reportedly his description in the Torah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r2.anchor: وقد ورد في صفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r3.claim: The sudden-result clause explains the benefit of the command: kindness can bring an enemy close to friendship and thus confirms the command's wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r3.anchor: وفرع على هذا الأمر قوله : { فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r4.claim: The prefixed “if/when” is suddenative, expressing the rapid appearance of kindness's effect in turning an enemy into a friend.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r4.anchor: وهي كناية عن سرعة ظهور أثر الدفع بالتي هي أحسن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r5.claim: The relative “one between you” permits an indefinite kind of enmity and a range of strength and duration; the rhetoric implies stronger kindness is needed against more entrenched hostility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p292/r5.anchor: وهذا تركيب من أعلى طرف البلاغة لأنه يجمع أحوال العداوات فيعلم أن الإحسان ناجع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r1.claim: The comparison means hostility has receded and affection has entered; the closeness varies and ordinarily does not reach full intimate friendship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r1.anchor: وجه الشبه هو المصافاة والمقاربة وهو معنى متفاوت الأحوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r2.claim: The enmity addressed is religious hostility from polytheism, so the verse does not describe hostility removed by conversion; ʿUmar and Hind illustrate that separate change.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r2.anchor: والعداوة التي بين المشركين وبين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عداوة في الدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r3.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about Abū Sufyān, once the Prophet's enemy and later a loyal friend after conversion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r3.anchor: وعن مقاتل : أنه قال : هذه الآية نزلت في أبي سفيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr accepts that Abū Sufyān later became friendly but doubts the verse was revealed about him, since it concerns winning affection through kindness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r4.anchor: فلا أحسب أن الآية نزلت في ذلك لأنها نزلت في اكتساب المودة بالإحسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r5.claim: Walī means ally or supporter, opposite an enemy; ḥamīm means close relative or friend, combining two qualities incompatible with enmity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p293/r5.anchor: والولي : اسم مشتق من الولاية بفتح الواو ، والولاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r3.claim: Good and evil are unequal; repeating wa-lā al-sayyiʾa emphasizes both directions of the comparison through ellipsis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r3.anchor: فقرر أن الحسنة والسيئة لا تستوي، أي فالحسنة أفضل، وكرر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r4.claim: The command gathers noble manners: meet social friction with the best conduct, including greeting, courtesy, controlling anger, and generosity in paying and collecting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ادفع بالتي هي أحسن آية جمعت مكارم الأخلاق وأنواع الحلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says these virtues protect a believer from Satan and humble the enemy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا فعل المؤمن هذه الفضائل عصمه الله من الشيطان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r6.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r6.claim: They explain the best response as greeting someone at a meeting; the author says greeting begins this wider practice but is only one part of it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r6.anchor: وفسر مجاهد وعطاء هذه الآية بالسلام عند اللقاء، ولا شك أن السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r7.claim: The simile says the enemy appears like a close friend, since a real enemy does not actually become one; his outward behavior only resembles a devoted friend.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r7.anchor: فدخل كاف التشبيه لأن الذي عنده عداوة لا يعود وليا حميما،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r8.claim: Ḥamīm is a close relative who cares for or protects a person; the pronoun in yulaqqāhā refers to the conduct implied by the command to respond best.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r8.anchor: والحميم: هو القريب الذي يحتم للإنسان. والضمير في قوله: يلقاها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r9.claim: The view that yulaqqāhā refers to the declaration lā ilāha illā Allāh is unsupported by the wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p16/r9.anchor: وقالت فرقة: المراد: وما يلقى لا إله إلا الله، وهذا تفسير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats the extra lā as emphatic, so the sense is that good and evil are not equal.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج لا زائدة مؤكدة والمعنى ولا تستوي الحسنة والسيئة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the good deed as faith and the evil deed as associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r2.anchor: أحدها أن الحسنة الإيمان والسيئة الشرك قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the contrast as forbearance versus obscenity.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r4.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits an interpretation of the contrast as fleeing versus patience.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r5.claim: Responding better means meeting anger with patience and harm with pardon; then an enemy becomes like a close friend.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r5.anchor: وذلك كدفع الغضب بالصبر والإساءة بالعفو فاذا فعلت ذلك صار الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كالصديق القريب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r6.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says to respond better by greeting an adversary with peace when meeting them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r6.anchor: قال عطاء هو السلام على من تعاديه إذا لقيته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r7.claim: The exegetes say this verse was abrogated by the sword verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p257/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون وهذه الآية منسوخة بآية السيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r1.claim: Good and evil differ greatly; answer an offender with kindness, which can turn enmity into close friendship, affection, and compassion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r1.anchor: من أساء إليك فادفعه عنك بالإحسان إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r2.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r2.claim: Umar says no response to someone disobeying God against you compares with obeying God in return.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p181/r2.anchor: ما عاقبت من عصى الله فيك بمثل أن تطيع الله فيه

JISHUMI:v9p6191/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6191/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6191/r4.claim: The passage teaches following evidence rather than leaders.
JISHUMI:v9p6191/r4.anchor: وتدل على وجوب اتباع الدليل دون الرؤساء

JISHUMI:v9p6191/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6191/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6191/r9.claim: Repeating “nor” either strengthens the negation as a poetic pleonasm or emphasizes that neither side equals the other.
JISHUMI:v9p6191/r9.anchor: وفي تكرير (لا) في قوله: (ولا السيئة) قولان

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r6.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r6.claim: One pairing is gentle accommodation as good and harshness as evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r6.anchor: الحسنة المداراة , والسيئة الغلظة , حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r7.claim: Another pairing is patience as good and aversion as evil.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r8.claim: He pairs faith with good and shirk with evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r8.anchor: الحسنة الإيمان , والسيئة الشرك , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r9.speaker: ابن عمير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r9.claim: He pairs forgiveness with good and retaliation with evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r9.anchor: الحسنة العفو والسيئة الانتصار , حكاه ابن عمير

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r10.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r10.claim: He pairs forbearance with good and obscenity with evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r10.anchor: الحسنة الحلم والسيئة الفحش , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r11.claim: He pairs love for the Prophet's family with good and hostility toward them with evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r11.anchor: الحسنة حب آل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والسيئة بغضهم , قاله علي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r12.claim: He says to answer an ignorant person's ignorance with forbearance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r12.anchor: ادفع بحلمك جهل من يجهل , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r13.speaker: عطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r13.claim: He says to answer an offender's harm with a peaceful response.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r13.anchor: ادفع بالسلامة إساءة المسيء , قاله عطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r14.claim: He also allows overlooking a sinner's offense; the lesser party commits a sin and the higher party shows clemency.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r14.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : ادفع بالتغافل إساءة المذنب

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r15.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r15.claim: He glosses a close ally as a friend and an intimate as a near relative.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r16.claim: One account says the verse addressed the Prophet's patience and forgiveness toward Abu Jahl, who had been harming him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p181/r16.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام كان يؤذي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم , فأمره بالصبر عليه والصفح عنه

MUQATIL:41:31-35/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:41:31-35/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:41:31-35/r3.claim: Because Abu Jahl harmed Muhammad, whom the Prophet disliked, God commanded forgiveness and forbearance; patience in restraining anger may turn an enemy into a close ally, and Muhammad must seek refuge from Satan.
MUQATIL:41:31-35/r3.anchor: وذلك أن أبا جهل كان يؤذي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكان النبي مبغضا له، يكره رؤيته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r1.claim: When two good responses are possible, take the better one to repel an enemy's harm: answer insult with praise and return a good deed for a bad one.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r1.anchor: فخذ بالحسنة التي هى احسن من اختها اذا اعترضتك حسنتان فادفع بها السيئة التي ترد عليك من بعض اعدائك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r2.claim: Such exceptional kindness can turn a hostile enemy into a close, affectionate friend.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p90#4/r2.anchor: فإنك اذا فعلت ذلك انقلب عدوك المشاق مثل الولى الحميم مصافاة لك

QURTUBI-FULL:41:33-34/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:33-34/r15.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:41:33-34/r15.claim: Al-Farra says the repeated negative particle is extra, so the phrase means good and evil are unequal.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:33-34/r15.anchor: قال الفراء: «لا» صلة أي «ولا تستوي الحسنة والسيئة»

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r1.claim: The cited poem about Abu Bakr and ʿUmar illustrates the contrast between monotheism and the polytheists' position.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r1.anchor: ما كان يرضى رسول الله فعلهم والطيبان أبو بكر ولا عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the good is “There is no god but God,” and the evil is polytheism.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الحسنة لا إله إلا الله، والسيئة الشرك.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r3.claim: Definitions pair obedience with idolatry, tact with harshness, and pardon with retaliation.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r3.anchor: وقيل: الحسنة المداراة، والسيئة الغلظة. وقيل: الحسنة العفو، والسيئة الانتصار.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r4.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak defines the good as knowledge and the evil as obscenity.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الحسنة العلم، والسيئة الفحش.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r5.claim: ʿAli identifies the good as love of the Prophet's family and the evil as hatred of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r5.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: الحسنة حب آل الرسول، والسيئة بغضهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r6.claim: The instruction to repel evil with what is better was abrogated by the fighting verse, though good company, forbearance, and overlooking remain recommended.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r6.anchor: نسخت بآية السيف، وبقي المستحب من ذلك: حسن العشرة والاحتمال والإغضاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the instruction as meeting another's ignorance with one's own forbearance.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي ادفع بحلمك جهل من يجهل عليك.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also gives a forgiving reply to an insult, asking God to forgive the other whether the charge is true or false.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r8.anchor: هو الرجل يسب الرجل فيقول الآخر إن كنت صادقا فغفر الله لي، وإن كنت كاذبا فغفر الله لك.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r9.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r9.claim: A report says Abu Bakr used this forgiving reply to a man who insulted him.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r9.anchor: وكذلك يروى في الأثر: أن أبا بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه قال ذلك لرجل نال منه.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r10.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r10.claim: Mujahid and ʿAta interpret the better response as greeting an enemy with peace.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «بالتي هي أحسن» يعني السلام إذا لقي من يعاديه وقاله عطاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r11.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r11.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi offers handshaking as another application, citing the saying that it removes rancor.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r11.anchor: وقول ثالث ذكره القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي في الأحكام وهو المصافحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r12.speaker: مالك وسفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r12.claim: Malik opposed handshaking and called the Prophet's greeting of Jaʿfar special; Sufyan argued that the Prophet's conduct applies to the community.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34/r12.anchor: فقال سفيان: قد صافح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جعفرا حين قدم من أرض الحبشة فقال له مالك: ذلك خاص.

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r1.claim: Al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib reports from the Prophet that two Muslims who meet and clasp hands in affection and sincere counsel have their sins fall away.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r1.anchor: ما من مسلمين يلتقيان فيأخذ أحدهما بيد صاحبه مودة بينهما ونصيحة إلا ألقيت ذنوبهما بينهما

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r2.claim: Muqatil says the former enemy who becomes a close friend was Abu Sufyan, who stopped harming the Prophet, became related by marriage, and entered Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: نزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب، كان مؤذيا للنبي

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r3.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi reports an alternative that the instruction concerned Abu Jahl, whom the Prophet was told to endure and pardon.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: هذه الآية نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام، كان يؤذي النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r4.claim: The author finds the Abu Sufyan report stronger because the verse describes an enemy becoming an intimate friend.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r4.anchor: والأول ذكره الثعلبي والقشيري وهو أظهر لقوله تعالى: { فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads the command as patience when angry, forbearance toward ignorance, and pardon for injury; this frustrates Satan and humbles enemies.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أمره الله تعالى في هذه الآية بالصبر عند الغضب، والحلم عند الجهل

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r6.claim: Ali tells Qanbar to ignore his abuser, please the Merciful, frustrate Satan, and punish a fool through silence.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r6.anchor: يا قنبر! دع شاتمك، واله عنه ترضي الرحمن وتسخط الشيطان

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r7.claim: An anonymous poem says refraining from insulting a vile person harms him more than returning the insult.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r7.anchor: وللكف عن شتم اللئيم تكرما أضر له من شتمه حين يشتم

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r8.claim: Another poem says silence is the answer that most frustrates a fool who insults a noble person.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r8.anchor: متاركة السفيه بلا جواب أشد على السفيه من السباب

QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r9.speaker: محمود الوراق
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r9.claim: Mahmud al-Warraq's poem advises honoring superiors, withholding a reply from inferiors, and showing forbearance to equals.
QURTUBI-FULL:41:34#2/r9.anchor: وقال محمود الوراق: سألزم نفسي الصفح عن كل مذنب

SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r1.claim: لا before السيئة may be extra for emphasis, as in the cited verses, because استوى requires two complements.
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r1.anchor:
في " لا " هذه وجهان، أحدهما، أنها زائدة للتوكيد، كقوله:
ولا الظل ولا الحرور

SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r2.claim: Alternatively لا is meaningful: حسنات and سيئات as classes are unequal internally, since individual good and evil acts differ in degree.
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها مؤسسة غير مؤكدة، إذ المراد بالحسنة والسيئة الجنس أي: لا تستوي الحسنات

SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r3.claim: He objects that if حسنات and سيئات are treated generically, the extra لا does not function like it did under the first analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r3.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " فإن أخذت الحسنة والسيئة جنسا لم تكن زيادتها كزيادتها في الوجه الذي قبل هذا

SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r4.claim: The author says the objection misreads the second analysis, which does not make لا extra.
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r4.anchor: قلت: فقد جعلها في المعنى الثاني زائدة. وفيه نظر لما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r5.claim: كأنه ولي may be a circumstantial clause: the preceding relative is subject and sudden إذا its predicate, with the central point that an enemy is present as an intimate friend.
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أنها في محل نصب على الحال، والموصول مبتدأ، و " إذا " التي للمفاجأة خبره

SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r6.claim: Alternatively the relative is subject and the following clause its predicate; إذا either attaches to the meaning of resemblance or is a particle with no governing element.
SAMIN-DURR:41:34/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن الموصول مبتدأ أيضا، والجملة بعده خبره، و " إذا " معمولة لمعنى التشبيه

RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r1.claim: Answer foolishness and ignorance with the best course: repeatedly endure bad manners without anger or retaliatory harm, until the offenders feel shame and abandon them.
RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r1.anchor: فإنك إذا صبرت على سوء أخلاقهم مرة بعد أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r2.claim: Meeting injury with kindness and bad acts with good turns enmity into love and hatred into affection.
RAZI-FULL:v27p110/r2.anchor: تركوا أفعالهم القبيحة وانقلبوا من العداوة إلى المحبة

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r1.claim: The command echoes 23:96, with 29:46 also relevant, and “better” can mean more beautiful or virtuous.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r1.anchor: Better can also mean “more beautiful” or “more virtuous.”

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r2.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r2.claim: Because “repel” has no stated object, one interpretation is to answer anger with patience.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r2.anchor: people should repel anger with patience (IJ)

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r3.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r3.claim: Another interpretation is to answer error with truth.

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r4.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r4.claim: Another interpretation is to answer ignorance with clemency.

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r5.speaker: IJ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r5.claim: Another interpretation is to answer wrongdoing with pardon.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r5.anchor: the commission of evil with pardon (IJ, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r6.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r6.claim: If others disobey God in their treatment of someone, that person should obey God in responding to them.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r6.anchor: if others disobey God in how they treat an individual, then that person should obey God in how he or she treats them (IK)

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r7.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r7.claim: Such conduct can produce reconciliation, love, and empathy.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r7.anchor: Such conduct can lead to reconciliation, love, and empathy (IK)

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r8.claim: Repaying evil with good does not require surrendering to an enemy or accepting falsehood; avoid returning harm when doing so will not cause greater harm.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r8.anchor: avoid reciprocating harm whenever such avoidance will not lead to greater evil

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r9.claim: A hadith treated as a foundational Islamic principle says there should be neither harm nor reciprocal harm.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r9.anchor: a ḥadīth taken by many as a foundational principle of Islam states, “Let there be no harming and no reciprocating harm.”

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r10.claim: Another hadith commends maintaining ties with those who sever them, giving to those who deny, and overlooking oppressors.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r10.anchor: Another states, “Keep relations with those who cut them off with you, give to those who deny you, and ignore those who oppress you.”

STUDYQURAN:41:34/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r11.claim: The command can also apply inwardly: repel one’s own base impulses toward vice by practicing virtue.
STUDYQURAN:41:34/r11.anchor: one should repel one’s own base tendencies toward vice by practicing virtue

TAB-FULL:v20p431/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r1.claim: Good conduct by believers who affirm God, obey, and invite others to obedience is unequal to the evil of those who reject the Quran and try to drown it out.
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r1.anchor: فكذلك لا تستوي عند الله أحوالهم ومنازلهم

TAB-FULL:v20p431/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r2.claim: The repeated negation is grammatically sound because if two things are not equal, each is unequal to the other; some Basran grammarians instead call the second “no” emphatic or redundant.

TAB-FULL:v20p431/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r3.claim: Some grammarians treat the repeated “no” as added emphasis, citing 57:29 and 75:2; another denies this, explaining the second negation as applying to the verb and saying the second “no” in 75:1 is a response before a fresh oath.
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r3.anchor: كما قال {لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب ألا يقدرون} [الحديد: 29] أي لأن يعلم، وكما قال: {لا أقسم بيوم القيامة ولا أقسم بالنفس اللوامة} [القيامة: 2]

TAB-FULL:v20p431/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r4.claim: The verse ultimately contrasts faith in God and obedience to Him with associating partners and disobeying Him.
TAB-FULL:v20p431/r4.anchor: ولا يستوي الإيمان بالله والعمل بطاعته والشرك به والعمل بمعصيته

TAB-FULL:v20p432/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r1.claim: Muhammad should meet ignorance with forbearance, answer offense with pardon, and patiently bear the harm he receives from opponents.
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ادفع بالتي هي أحسن} [فصلت: 34] قال: «أمر الله المؤمنين بالصبر عند الغضب

TAB-FULL:v20p432/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers should remain patient when angry, show forbearance and pardon when wronged; this protects them from Satan and humbles an enemy into a close ally.
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ادفع بالتي هي أحسن} [فصلت: 34] قال: «أمر الله المؤمنين بالصبر عند الغضب

TAB-FULL:v20p432/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r3.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r3.claim: Ata interprets the better response to offense as greeting the offender with peace; Mujahid gives the greeting as “peace be upon you” when meeting.
TAB-FULL:v20p432/r3.anchor: عن طلحة بن عمرو، عن عطاء {ادفع بالتي هي أحسن} [فصلت: 34] قال: «بالسلام»

TAB-FULL:v20p433/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p433/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p433/r1.claim: Responding to an offender with the commanded goodness can turn an enemy into a kindly close ally or near relative; hamim means close kin.
TAB-FULL:v20p433/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {كأنه ولي حميم} [فصلت: 34] «أي كأنه ولي قريب»

TAB-FULL:v20p433/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p433/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p433/r2.claim: Qatada glosses “a warm ally” as a close ally or relative.
TAB-FULL:v20p433/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {كأنه ولي حميم} [فصلت: 34] «أي كأنه ولي قريب»

ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r9.claim: The second lā is emphatic and extra; the sense is that good and evil are not equal.
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r9.anchor: زائدة مؤكدة، المعنى لا تستوي والسيئة.

ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r10.claim: The command means to repel an evil deed with what is better.
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r10.anchor: معناه ادفع السيئة بالتي هي أحسن

ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p385/r11.claim: Ḥamīm means a close relative or intimate.

TABATABAI:41:33-35/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r5.claim: After praising the call to God, the passage addresses the Prophet about the best way to invite people and make the greatest impact on them.
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r5.anchor: ببيان أحسن الطريق إلى الدعوة وأقربها من الغاية المطلوبة منها وهي التأثير في النفوس

TABATABAI:41:33-35/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r6.claim: Good and evil mean good and bad conduct in their effect on people; the extra negative particle in nor the evil intensifies the denial of equality.
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r6.anchor: أي الخصلة الحسنة والسيئة من حيث حسن التأثير في النفوس،

TABATABAI:41:33-35/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r7.claim: Repel an opposing bad act with the better response: truth for falsehood, forbearance for ignorance, and forgiveness for injury.
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r7.anchor: ادفع بالخصلة التي هي أحسن الخصلة السيئة التي تقابلها وتضادها فادفع بالحق الذي عندك باطلهم لا بباطل آخر وبحلمك جهلهم وبعفوك إساءتهم

TABATABAI:41:33-35/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r8.claim: Answering evil with the better response can transform an enemy into someone like a devoted, affectionate friend.
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r8.anchor: بيان لأثر الدفع بالأحسن ونتيجته، والمراد أنك إن دفعت بالتي هي أحسن فاجأك أن عدوك صار كأنه ولي شفيق.

TABATABAI:41:33-35/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:41:33-35/r9.claim: One view says that describing the person with whom one has enmity is more eloquent than simply saying enemy, while also being concise.

TABRISI:41:34-35/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:34-35/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:34-35/r6.claim: Good and evil may mean Islam and unbelief, righteous and wicked deeds, or opposing traits such as patience and anger, forbearance and ignorance, tact and harshness, pardon and injury.
TABRISI:41:34-35/r6.anchor: لا تستوي الخصلة الحسنة والسيئة فلا يستوي الصبر والغضب والحلم والجهل

TABRISI:41:34-35/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:34-35/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:34-35/r7.claim: The Prophet is told to answer opponents' falsehood with truth, their ignorance with forbearance, and their injury with pardon.
TABRISI:41:34-35/r7.anchor: ادفع بحقك باطلهم وبحلمك جهلهم وبعفوك إساءتهم

TABRISI:41:34-35/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:34-35/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:34-35/r8.claim: Gentle, patient forbearance can turn an enemy in religion into someone resembling an intimate ally in faith and kinship.
TABRISI:41:34-35/r8.anchor: صار عدوك الذي يعاديك في الدين بصورة وليك القريب

TABRISI:41:34-35/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:34-35/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:41:34-35/r9.claim: Abu ʿAbd Allāh identifies the good deed as taqiyya and the bad deed as disclosure.
TABRISI:41:34-35/r9.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله ع أن الحسنة التقية والسيئة الإذاعة

TABRISI:41:34-35/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:41:34-35/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:41:34-35/r15.claim: The passage contrasts the unbelievers' effort to drown out Qurʾan recitation with Muhammad's unsurpassed call to their acknowledged Creator; his practice matches his teaching and removes suspicion.
TABRISI:41:34-35/r15.anchor: ولا قائل أحسن قولا من محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعوكم إلى من تقرون أنه خالقكم

ASAD-NOTES:41:33#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:41:33#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:41:33#n31/r1.claim: The command to repel evil with what is better refers here to scurrilous objections and hostile criticism of the Qur’an; the passage continues the argument of verse 26 and parallels 13:22 note 44.
ASAD-NOTES:41:33#n31/r1.anchor: the injunction to "repel [evil] with something that is better" relates to scurrilous objections to, and hostile criticism of, the Qur'an

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:34-38/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:34-38/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:41:34-38/r1.claim: The negative particle in “good and evil are not equal” is redundant; answer evil with better: anger with patience, ignorance with forbearance, and injury with pardon, making an enemy a close friend.

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r1.claim: Good and evil are not equal, and neither are all good acts or all evil acts; their effects and degrees vary.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r1.anchor: her hasene de bir olmaz, her seyyie de; hem güzel huyların, iyi amellerin âsâr ve ahkâmda mertebeleri muhteliftir

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r2.claim: When inviting to God, one should avoid intensifying wrongdoing and repel evil with the best treatment or the finest form of the call to God.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r2.anchor: Emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’lmünker ile Allah’a davet yapılırken kötülüklerin teşdîdine

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r3.claim: The best way to counter evil is the call to God joined to righteous action, especially answering wrongdoing with kindness, which is better than mere pardon or patience.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r3.anchor: amel-i sâlihin en güzeli de kötülüğe karşı iyiliktir ki mücerred aftan, sabırdan daha güzeldir

ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r4.claim: Elmalılı cites Abu Sufyan as an example of an enemy becoming a close, compassionate ally.
ELMALILI:41:33-39#2/r4.anchor: Denilmiştir ki nitekim Ebû Süfyan öyle oldu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r1.speaker: Zemahşerî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r1.claim: Forgiving an offender is good, but repaying the harm with kindness is better and can turn an implacable enemy into a close friend.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r1.anchor: onu affetmen bir iyiliktir; ama bundan da iyi olanı, onun sana yaptığı kötülüğe iyilikle karşılık vermendir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r2.claim: In context, goodness means the Messenger's call to true religion, patience with insolent deniers, and refusal to seek revenge or answer evil with evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r2.anchor: Resûlullah’ın insanları hak dine davet etmesi, inkârcıların küstahça davranışlarına sabretmesi, intikam peşinde koşmaması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r3.claim: The evil refers to idolaters' degrading rejection of the message, including saying their hearts are closed and urging noise while the Qur'an is recited.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r3.anchor: “Bizi çağırdığın şeylere karşı kalplerimiz kapalıdır” (5. âyet); “Bu Kur’an’a kulak vermeyin, okunurken gürültü çıkarın” (26. âyet)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r4.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r4.claim: The verse distinguishes the Messenger's fitting goodness from their evil: goodness merits respect in this world and reward in the next, so their conduct must not stop him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r4.anchor: İyilikle kötülük bir olmaz; yani eğer sen iyilik yaparsan dünyada saygınlığı, âhirette de sevabı hak edersin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r5.claim: Persistently answering barbarous and ignorant behavior with patience rather than anger or retaliation may eventually shame opponents into abandoning it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r5.anchor: utanır, o çirkin davranışlarını da artık terk ederler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r11.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r11.claim: He says the instruction encompasses all virtues of character and forms of forbearance, including greeting, restraining anger, and making debts easier; Ibn Abbas says such a believer is protected from Satan and gains an enemy's respect.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:41:34/r11.anchor: “bütün ahlâk güzelliklerini ve hilim çeşitlerini” kapsadığını belirtir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r4.claim: The Prophet carries a noble call and should answer ignorant opposition with decency and forgiveness, a difficult but wise approach attained through patience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p62/r4.anchor: he should counter their ignorance with decency and forgiveness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p81/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p81/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p81/r3.claim: The Prophet should patiently forgive naïve opponents who disrupt the blessed message; this gracious response benefits his preaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p81/r3.anchor: he should patiently forgive this misdemeanour. This gracious behaviour from him will bring great benefit and blessings to his preaching endeavour.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p86/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p86/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p86/r5.claim: Good and bad conduct produce sharply different effects and consequences for both the Hereafter and the goals of preaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p86/r5.anchor: There is a world of difference between the effect and consequences of both

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r1.claim: Although equal retaliation is permitted, forgiveness and patience are better in God's sight and more effective for preaching and reform.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r1.anchor: though it is permitted to a person to exact an equal revenge for an excess committed against him, yet forgiveness and showing patience is even better

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r2.claim: Qur'an 16:125–126 calls for wise, kindly, best-mannered preaching and allows proportionate retaliation while naming patience the better course.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r2.anchor: And if you exercise patience, then this is the best way for the patient.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r3.claim: Patience and forgiveness are the better response while truth is still being conclusively conveyed; after rejection and active efforts to destroy believers and their message, taking opponents to task can become better or necessary.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r3.anchor: the believers are directed to adopt this behaviour until the truth is conclusively conveyed to their opponents

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r4.claim: The Meccans urged to forgive in this verse were later punished by the Companions at God's direction once the truth had been conclusively conveyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r4.anchor: the very people of Makkah with whom the Almighty urged the Prophet (sws) and his companions to adopt the attitude of forgiveness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r5.claim: The enemy's change into a close friend reflects human nature: even one initially moved by hostility can be touched by a person's persistent wish for their good despite mistreatment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p87/r5.anchor: When people whose nature has not been perverted see that so anxious is a person in wishing well for them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p88/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p88/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p88/r1.claim: Magnanimous conduct turns some opponents' hostility into affection; Muhammad's character was a leading force in his preaching, winning sincere companions from those with decency, while hardened hearts remained unmoved.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p88/r1.anchor: the most effective factor in the preaching mission of Mu ḥammad (sws) was this aspect of his character

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains repelling evil with what is better as greeting the person with peace when meeting him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ادفع بالتي هي أحسن ﴾ قال السلام سلم عليه إذ لقيته

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r2.claim: Qatada explains ‘a close, affectionate friend’ as a close relative or ally.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p187#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كأنه ولي حميم ﴾ قال ولي قريب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r9.claim: Because a person who calls others to God may face hostility, he should convey good gently and tactfully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r9.anchor: وأن الداعي إلى الله قد يجافيه المدعو، فينبغي أن يرفق به ويتلطف في إيصال الخير فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r10.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about Abu Sufyan, an enemy of the Messenger who became a close friend.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r10.anchor: قيل: ونزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب، وكان عدوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فصار وليا مصافيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r11.claim: He identifies the good as saying “There is no god but God” and the evil as associating partners with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الحسنة لا إله إلا الله، والسيئة الشرك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r12.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r12.claim: He takes the contrast to be the two rival invitations: to monotheism and to associationism.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r13.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p305/r13.claim: He explains good and evil as forbearance and obscenity.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r1.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r1.claim: He identifies good and evil as love of the Messenger and his family versus hatred of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r1.anchor: وعن علي: حب الرسول وآله وبغضهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r2.claim: Other illustrative contrasts are patience versus aversion, leniency versus harshness, and pardon versus moderation; these examples are not exhaustive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r2.anchor:
وقيل:
الصبر والنفور. وقيل: المداراة والغلظة. وقيل: العفو والاقتصاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r3.claim: The order “repel with what is better” intensifies the command: whoever finds superior repayment easy will find merely good repayment easy too.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r3.anchor: ولما تفاوتت الحسنة والسيئة، أمر أن يدفع السيئة بالأحسن، وذلك مبالغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r4.claim: He says كأن marks a comparison because an actual enemy does not become an intimate ally, though he may seem one outwardly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r4.anchor: لأن الذي عنده عداوة لا يعود وليا حميما، وإنما يحسن ظاهره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r5.claim: He identifies the better response as patience when angry, forbearance when treated ignorantly, and forgiving injury.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: بالتي هي أحسن: الصبر عند الغضب، والحلم عند الجهل، والعفو عند الإساءة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r6.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r6.claim: They say the better response begins with greeting the opponent on meeting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد، وعطاء: السلام عند اللقاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r7.claim: Greeting at a meeting is only the beginning of the superior response, not its full extent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r7.anchor: أي هو مبدأ الدفع بالأحسن، لأنه محصور فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r8.claim: He also recommends turning away from their harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r8.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا: أعرض عن أذاهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r9.speaker: أبو فراس الحمداني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r9.claim: His poem commends continual patient forgiveness as the best response to injury.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p306/r9.anchor: يجني علي وأجنو صافحا أبدا ... لا شيء أحسن من جان على جان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r1.claim: The independent sentence encourages the Messenger to endure polytheist abuse and answer harm with good; generally, good and evil deeds differ in effects and rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r1.anchor: سيقت لبيان محاسن الأعمال الجارية بين العباد أثر بيان محاسن الأعمال الجارية بين العبد والرب

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r2.claim: The second negative particle is extra for emphasis, as in the verse denying equality of shade and heat.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r2.anchor: الثانية مزيدة لتأكيد النفي مثلها في قوله تعالى ( ولا الظل ولا الحرور )

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r3.claim: Repel any evil from an enemy with a better response, such as doing good to an offender, which surpasses merely forgiving; “better” has a general omitted comparator.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r3.anchor: ادفع السيئة حيث اعترضك من بعض أعاديك بالتي هي أحسن منها وهي الحسنة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r4.claim: The wording “better” instead of simply “good” signals that lesser goodness will then be easy; the question-and-answer form stresses that this is a matter to ask and heed.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r4.anchor: عن سؤال من قال : كيف أصنع للمبالغة والإشارة إلى أنه مهم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r5.claim: Alusi says the good and evil are not two particular acts; the authorial reading is a general moral instruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r5.anchor: ومما ذكرنا يعلم أن ليس المراد بالحسنة والسيئة أمرين معينين

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r6.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r6.claim: Ali interprets the good as love for the Messenger and his family, and the evil as hatred of them.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r6.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه حب الرسول وآله عليهم الصلاة والسلام والسيئة بغضهم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the good as the declaration that there is no god but God and the evil as associating partners with Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الحسنة لا إله إلا الله والسيئة الشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r8.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets the terms as the two invitations to monotheism and associationism.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الدعوتان إليهما وقال الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak reads the contrast as forbearance versus obscenity.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك : الحلم والفحش وقيل : الصبر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r10.claim: Other reported glosses include patience and leniency versus harshness; Alusi doubts some are intended here or reliably transmitted from their named authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r10.anchor: لا يخفى أن بعض المروي يكاد لا تصح إرادته هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r11.claim: A second grammatical reading takes both terms as generic classes whose individual deeds vary from good to better and evil to worse; the second la then is not extra, and the command means answer the worse evil with the best good.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123/r11.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد بيان تفاوت الحسنات والسيئات في أنفسهما

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r1.claim: The commanded response can make a hostile person resemble a compassionate friend.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r1.anchor: بيان لنتيجة الدفع المأمور به فإذا فعلت ذلك صار عدوك المشاق مثل الولي الشفيق

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the simile is necessary because answering well often makes an enemy appear friendly without turning him into a true intimate.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية : دخلت ( كأن ) المفيدة للتشبيه لأن العدو لا يعود وليا حميما

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r3.claim: Alusi says this may state only the usual minimum result; sometimes good responses dissolve hostility altogether, as an anonymous verse says.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r3.anchor: وإلا فقد تزول العداوة بالكلية بذلك كما قيل إن العداوة تستحيل مودة بتدارك الفهوات بالحسنات

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r4.claim: The wording the one between you and whom there is enmity is more expressive than your enemy, though longer, and so was rhetorically chosen.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r4.anchor: أبلغ من عدوك ولذا اختير عليه مع اختصاره

ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r5.claim: Some say the verse was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan, once the Messenger enemy and later a close friend to Sunnis; Alusi adds a sharp aside about his grandson Yazid.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p123#2/r5.anchor: فصار عند أهل السنة وليا مصافيا وكأن ما عنده انتقل إلى ولد ولده يزيد عليه من الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r1.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r1.claim: Al-Farra says the negative particle is extra here: good and evil are not equal, such as patience versus anger, forbearance versus ignorance, and pardon versus wrongdoing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: "لا" هاهنا صلة، معناه: ولا تستوي الحسنة والسيئة، يعني الصبر والغضب، والحلم والجهل، والعفو والإساءة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says to answer anger with patience, ignorance with forbearance, and offense with pardon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أمر بالصبر عند الغضب، وبالحلم عند الجهل، وبالعفو عند الإساءة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r3.claim: Responding in this way humbles an enemy until the former enemy becomes a close friend and relative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r3.anchor: فعلت ذلك خضع لك عدوك، وصار الذي بينك وبينه عداوة، {كأنه ولي حميم}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r4.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says the verse was revealed about Abu Sufyan, who softened after hostility through marriage ties with the Prophet and later became a close ally through Islam and kinship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p174/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل بن حيان: نزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب، وذلك أنه لان للمسلمين بعد شدة عداوته

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r1.claim: Good and evil are unequal in recompense and outcome; the second lā reinforces the negation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r1.anchor: في الجزاء وحسن العاقبة و { لا } الثانية مزيدة لتأكيد النفي

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r2.claim: Answer an encountered evil with better goodness, or the best possible good response; presenting it as an answer to how to act intensifies the command and substitutes better for goodness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r2.anchor: ادفع السيئة حيث اعترضتك بالتي هي أحسن منها وهي الحسنة

BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r3.claim: This response may transform a hostile enemy into a compassionate close friend.
BAYDAWI-FULL:41:34-35/r3.anchor: صار عدوك المشاق مثل الولي الشفيق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r1.claim: Good and evil differ both among acts of the same kind and in their agents’ intentions and effort; this comparison urges people toward good and away from evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r1.anchor: أي وإن اجتهدت في التحرير والاعتبار

BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r2.claim: One should repel whatever harm may come from oneself or others with the best attainable conduct; forgiving an offender is good, while responding with benevolence is better.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r2.anchor: أي كل ما يمكن أن يضرك من نفسك ومن الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r3.claim: Such excellent treatment can turn even a bitter enemy into a close friend who readily meets needs, eases difficulties, heals hurts, and removes what is foul, like hot water cleansing dirt.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p572/r3.anchor: عظيمة قد ملأت ما بين البنيين فاجأته حال كونه

JISHUMI:v9p6192/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6192/r6.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v9p6192/r6.claim: Muqātil says the verse about an enemy becoming a close friend was revealed concerning Abū Sufyān, who harmed the Prophet and later became his son-in-law through Ramlah, Umm Ḥabība.
JISHUMI:v9p6192/r6.anchor: وعن مقاتل أن قوله: (فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم) نزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب كان يؤذي رسول الله، ثم صار له وليا وصهرا

JISHUMI:v9p6192/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6192/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6192/r7.claim: The author rejects Muqātil’s occasion report: the verse does not support it, Abū Sufyān was never truly an ally, and his hostile remarks and incitement against Abū Bakr exposed his deception.
JISHUMI:v9p6192/r7.anchor: وليس في الظاهر ما يدل عليه، وأبو سفيان لم يكن وليا قط، وقد قال يوم عثمان: إني لأرجو أن يعود ديننا

RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r10.claim: The verses command answering evil with what is better and seeking refuge when Satan provokes; Razi says they show prophets continually sought protection from evil human and jinn devils.
RAZI-FULL:v1p67#2/r10.anchor: فهذه الآيات دالة على أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام كانوا أبدا في الاستعاذة من شر شياطين الإنس والجن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r1.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r1.claim: Al-Jurjani argues that verbal argument needs a receptive listener; rhetorical merits remain elusive, with fine features emerging after prolonged study and rereading.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r1.anchor: ومضى "الجرجاني" بعد أن أتم توجيه البلاغة لتكون علم الاستدلال للإعجاز

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati says al-Jurjani shifted inquiry into rhetoric apart from the Quran, guiding later scholars to study rhetoric independently in hopes of explaining Quranic inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r2.anchor: نقل القضية نقلة حاسمة إلى ميدان الدرس البلاغي بمعزل عن القرآن نفسه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r3.speaker: أبو نواس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r3.claim: Abu Nuwas's poem portrays the struggle to interpret a visible image: suspicion displaces certainty, and understanding remains incomplete.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p128/r3.anchor: كما قال أبّو نواس: ألا لا أرى مثل امترائىَ في رسم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r1.claim: A poem's proposition may be plain and shared rather than poetic in itself; poetry contributes its wording, expression, brevity or expansion, and manner of disclosure.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r1.anchor: صريح معنى ليس للشعر في جوهره وذاته نصيب وإنما له ما يلبسه من اللفظ ويكسوه من العبارة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r2.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r2.claim: The maxim that everyone who does good is loved derives from the Prophetic saying that hearts are naturally disposed to love whoever treats them well.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r2.anchor: وأصله قول النبي جبلت القلوب على حب من أحسن إليها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r3.claim: Jurjani adduces God's command to answer in the best manner, so that an enemy becomes a close friend, as a Qur'anic parallel to the maxim.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r3.anchor: إدفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r4.claim: The line that lofty honor is not safe from harm until blood is shed expresses a rational truth affirmed by statesmen and enacted in divine commands, legal rulings, and Prophetic practice.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r4.anchor: لا يسلم الشرف الرفيع من الأذى حتى يراق على جوانبه الدم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r5.claim: Tyrants and defiant opponents cannot be checked by wisdom, advice, or awareness of injustice; only the pain of steel and force restrains them, preserving religion and worldly order.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r5.anchor: كالبهائم والسباع لا يوجعهم إلا ما يخرق الأبشار من حد الحديد وسطو البأس الشديد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r6.claim: Jurjani illustrates the need to repel harm by comparing it to clearing dirt from a well and illness from a body.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p229/r6.anchor: فلا يطيب الشرب من منهل لم تنف عنه الأقذاء ولا تقر الروح في بدن لم تدفع عنه الأدواء

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r1.claim: Some likenesses need no interpretation, such as a cheek and rose alike in redness; their resemblance is directly sensed.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r1.anchor: وأي تأول يجرى في مشابهة الخد للورد في الحمرة وأنت تراها ههنا كما تراها هناك

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r2.claim: A second kind of likeness depends on interpretation; the example is an argument likened to the sun in its manifestness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r2.anchor: ومثال الثاني وهو الشبه الذي يحصل بضرب من التأول كقولك هذه حجة كالشمس في الظهور

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r3.claim: A doubt functions as a mental barrier just as a curtain blocks physical sight; removing doubt lets the heart apprehend the proof.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r3.anchor: أن الشبهة نظير الحجاب فيما يدرك بالعقول لأنها تمنع القلب رؤية ما هي شبهة فيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r4.claim: Once an objection is removed, a proof is manifest like the sun; its denier has no excuse, being either unsound in reason or stubbornly obstinate.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r4.anchor: كما أن الشمس الطالعة لا يشك فيها ذو بصر ولا ينكرها إلا من لا عذر له في إنكاره

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r5.claim: Interpretive likenesses range from nearly effortless comparisons to subtle ones that require reflection and delicate thought.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p72/r5.anchor: ومنه ما يدق ويغمض حتى يحتاج في استخراجه إلى فضل روية ولطف فكره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r1.claim: Phrases saying a meaning outruns its wording or enters the ear unbidden concern an inference from one meaning to another, not the fixed lexical mapping of a known language.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r1.anchor: أنه لا يخلو السامع من أن يكون عالما باللغة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r2.claim: Eloquence makes an initial meaning a clear, low-effort intermediary to a second meaning, so the listener reaches the implication quickly as if it came directly from the wording.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r2.anchor: وأنهم أرادوا أن من شرط البلاغة أن يكون المعنى الأول

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r3.claim: Jurjānī classifies “لا أمتع العوذ بالفصال” as a metonymy example illustrating how a first meaning points toward a further meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r3.anchor: لا أمتع العوذ بالفصال ولا أبتاع إلا قريبة الأجل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r4.claim: Jurjānī cites “وصدر أراح الليل عازب همه” as an example of metaphor, where the wording leads from an expressed meaning to an implied one.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r4.anchor: وصدر أراح الليل عازب همه تضاعف فيه الحزن

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r5.claim: Jurjānī cites “لا أذود الطير عن شجر” as an example of representation, illustrating indirect meaning through an image.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p207/r5.anchor: لا أذود الطير عن شجر قد بلوت المر من ثمره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r1.claim: Critics trust their own taste and answer criticism by asserting their perception is sounder, so argument cannot persuade someone unwilling to reconsider his judgment.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r2.claim: Persuasion requires a listener able to overcome his own instinct and hear the argument; that receptivity can turn initial rejection into acceptance.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r3.claim: Even strenuous analysis leaves doubts about this subtle subject; Jurjānī invokes Abū Nuwās to illustrate how certainty can seem close yet remain unsettled.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p397/r3.anchor: كنت الذي لا يزال يتراءى لك فيه شبهة
